skill.name: azure-rbac
skill.description: Helps select least-privilege Azure RBAC roles for identities, then drafts Azure CLI commands and Bicep role assignment snippets.
skill.summary: Select least-privilege Azure RBAC roles and generate assignment guidance.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: No static findings were reported for this prompt-only skill. Review of SKILL.md found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or social engineering content.

content.value_statement: Azure role assignments are easy to over-permission. This skill helps select least-privilege roles and draft Azure CLI and Bicep assignment steps.
actual_capabilities: Looks up Azure RBAC role definitions for requested permissions.
Suggests minimal built-in roles when one matches the access need.
Requests a custom role definition when built-in roles do not fit.
Generates Azure CLI commands for role assignment workflows.
Provides Bicep snippets for role assignments and related best practices.
limitations: Does not create or configure managed identities.
Does not perform broad Azure security hardening.
Depends on Azure documentation and tool responses available in the host agent.
Generated commands require review against tenant policies and target scope.

use_cases.title: Assign Storage Access
use_cases.description: Find the narrowest role for an identity that needs read or write access to Azure Storage.

use_cases.title: Automate Role Assignments
use_cases.description: Draft Azure CLI commands and Bicep snippets for repeatable infrastructure deployments.

use_cases.title: Review Least Privilege
use_cases.description: Compare requested permissions with built-in roles before approving access changes.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Role
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the least-privilege Azure RBAC role for a user who needs read-only access to one storage account.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Assignment Steps
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend the minimal RBAC role for a managed identity that reads blobs, then draft Azure CLI assignment steps.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Built-In Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether a built-in Azure RBAC role covers starting and stopping virtual machines without granting broader compute permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Custom Role
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a custom role plan for an app that can read Key Vault secrets and list vault metadata at resource-group scope.

output_examples.input: A managed identity needs to read blobs in one container.
output_examples.output: Recommends Storage Blob Data Reader at container scope and explains why broader storage roles are unnecessary.

output_examples.input: An operator needs to restart virtual machines but not change networking.
output_examples.output: Identifies the closest built-in role, notes permission gaps, and suggests custom role guidance if needed.

output_examples.input: A deployment needs Bicep for assigning a role at resource-group scope.
output_examples.output: Provides a role assignment plan with required identity, role definition, scope, and validation notes.

best_practices: State the target identity, resource type, scope, and required actions.
Ask for built-in role comparison before requesting a custom role.
Review generated commands with Azure policy and change-control requirements.
anti_patterns: Requesting Owner or Contributor access for convenience.
Using subscription scope when resource scope is enough.
Treating generated commands as approved production changes.

faq.question: Can this skill assign Azure roles directly?
faq.answer: No. It drafts commands and Bicep snippets for review and execution in your environment.

faq.question: Does it support managed identities?
faq.answer: Yes. It can recommend RBAC roles for managed identities, but it does not create them.

faq.question: Can it create custom roles?
faq.answer: It can draft a custom role definition when built-in roles do not match the requested permissions.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the identity type, desired actions, resource type, Azure scope, and any policy constraints.

faq.question: Does it replace security review?
faq.answer: No. Review all generated role assignments against organizational policy before use.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
